exposure: skin-to-skin contact for 2 hours without interruption after birth
artificial milk supplements for the newborn
outcome: nipple soreness (measured by Visual Analogue Scale (VAS))
cohort: The study surveyed 58 mothers on their second postpartum day at the Infanta Cristina University Hospital in Madrid, Spain.
finding: The prevalence of nipple soreness at 48 hours postpartum was 97%, with a significant finding that a higher LATCH score was associated with less pain, and prolonged skin-to-skin contact was related to a higher pain score.
mod_finding: No association was found between nipple soreness (VAS) and the type of birth.
